title: Pre-Analysis — Release of the Chromate-Free Surface Protection Standard to In-Service Structural Work
abstract: Pre-analysis of the step from a production surface protection standard to one usable on in-service structural work, covering process approval at repair stations, the standard practices content and the structural candidates that already assume it.

sections.objective: Establish what stands between a surface protection standard that is cut into the production line and the same standard being usable by a repair station on an aircraft in service. The driver is regulatory rather than technical: the hexavalent process it replaces is being withdrawn, and every structural change now in pre-analysis has written its substantiation around the replacement. The question is whether the process, the coupon regime and the published standard practices content can reach the network before the withdrawal date.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and none of them is a design problem; all four are about reach. The standard practices bulletin that carries the process to the network is written as an information release rather than an instruction, so a station reading it has no obligation to hold the coupon regime that the adhesion data depends on. The surface preparation and application task in the standard practices manual describes the process correctly but does not state a shelf life for the mixed conversion solution, which is the single most common cause of a failed coupon. The corrosion removal and restoration task still calls the withdrawn process by name in its restoration step. A structural candidate in pre-analysis has already declared the new standard as a prerequisite on every new faying surface it creates, which fixes the date by which the network has to be ready.
sections.next_steps: Convert the standard practices bulletin from an information release into a recommended bulletin carrying the coupon regime as an instruction. Add the mixed solution shelf life to the application task and re-issue it in the next manual batch. Raise a change request against the corrosion restoration task so that it names the replacement process. Give the structural candidate's pre-analysis a written station readiness date so that it can state its prerequisite with a date attached rather than as an open condition.

similarity_seeds: conversion coating released for in-service structural repair
adhesion coupon regime and station process approval
withdrawal of a hexavalent surface treatment

tasks.title: Review the standard practices bulletin against network obligations
Sweep standard practices manual content for the withdrawn process
Identify structural candidates that already assume the new standard
Confirm coupon regime feasibility with three network stations

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin releases the process to the network as information. The adhesion data that every structural substantiation rests on assumes a per-shift coupon regime, and an information release gives a station no obligation to run it.
expected_findings.resolution: Re-issue the bulletin as a recommended bulletin with the coupon regime written as an instruction.

expected_findings.rationale: The surface preparation and application task describes the process correctly but gives no shelf life for the mixed conversion solution. Over-age solution is the commonest cause of a failed coupon and the task as written does not prevent it.
expected_findings.resolution: Add the mixed solution shelf life and a discard instruction to the task.

expected_findings.rationale: The corrosion removal and restoration task still names the withdrawn treatment in its restoration step. Once the treatment is unavailable the task cannot be completed as written, and the aircraft is left with bare prepared metal.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a change request naming the replacement process and its cure condition in the restoration step.

expected_findings.rationale: The lap joint candidate has already declared the new standard as a condition on every faying surface it creates. Its retrofit window therefore depends on the station readiness date this analysis has to produce.
expected_findings.resolution: Issue a written station readiness date to the candidate's pre-analysis so it can state a dated prerequisite.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned by both passes because it is a corrosion repair that references the standard practices chapter, but it concerns the windshield frame sealing land in the cockpit. It shares no part number and no zone with the fuselage and wing joints this standard covers, and its protection scheme is specified by the repair itself.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a positive position. The process is sound and the remaining work is publication and network obligation rather than design; a station readiness date was issued to the dependent candidate.
